title: John Bew on British Realpolitik
gist: In an EI Podcast with Jack Dickens, King's College London historian and former prime-ministerial adviser John Bew argues the UK is in a difficult but not hopeless strategic position: everything in the international order is being renegotiated, so properly funded armed forces are a bargaining asset; Britain's open economy makes it uniquely exposed to Middle East energy and shipping shocks; and, against conventional wisdom, hard transatlantic metrics (FDI, trade, US defence purchases) have never been stronger even as Europe's politics fragment. He draws lessons from Attlee and Bevin's hard-headed postwar statecraft.
